ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a fused bicyclic skeleton, with a six-membered ring containing one C=C double bond on the left, and a saturated six-membered ring on the right; the two rings share one vertical bridge bond. The lower-left alkenyl carbon is connected downward to a negatively charged oxygen, namely O⁻. The upper bridgehead carbon is connected to a peroxide/hydroperoxy substituent, shown as C–O–O–H. There are also multiple curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring these arrows and looking only at the static connectivity. Reasoning: Convert the structure into a molecular graph according to the static connectivity: starting from the negatively charged oxygen, it is single-bonded to an alkenyl carbon, which can be written as [O-]C1. This alkenyl carbon forms a double bond with the adjacent ring-fusion carbon, written as [O-]C1=C2. Traversing along the right saturated six-membered ring to the upper bridgehead carbon gives CCCCC2; this bridgehead carbon bears an OOH substituent, written as C2(OO). Then along the remaining three carbons of the left ring back to the starting alkenyl carbon, written as CCC1. Therefore the corresponding SMILES is [O-]C1=C2CCCCC2(OO)CCC1.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First describe the image, then reason from the static connectivity. Ignore all curved arrows as instructed. Convert the drawn skeleton into a molecular graph: an anionic oxygen is single-bonded to a vinylic carbon; that carbon is double-bonded to a ring-fusion carbon; continue around the right cyclohexane to the upper bridgehead carbon, which carries an OOH substituent; then continue around the left ring back to the starting vinylic carbon. Assign SMILES ring numbers to close the two fused rings, yielding a valid expression: [O-]C1=C2CCCCC2(OO)CCC1.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个稠合双环骨架，左侧为含一个 C=C 双键的六元环，右侧为饱和六元环，两环共用一条竖直的桥键。左下方的烯基碳向下连接一个带负电的氧，即 O⁻。上方桥头碳连接一个过氧/氢过氧取代基，表现为 C–O–O–H。图中还有多条弯箭头，但题目要求忽略这些箭头，只看静态连接关系。
推理：按静态连接把结构转为分子图：从带负电的氧开始，它单键连接到一个烯基碳，可写作 [O-]C1。该烯基碳与相邻的环融合碳形成双键，写作 [O-]C1=C2。沿右侧饱和六元环绕行到上方桥头碳，得到 CCCCC2；该桥头碳带有 OOH 取代基，写作 C2(OO)。随后沿左侧环的其余三个碳回到起始烯基碳，写作 CCC1。因此对应的 SMILES 为 [O-]C1=C2CCCCC2(OO)CCC1。
